# gptr <picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Broccolito/gptr/main/man/figures/logo-dark.png"/><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Broccolito/gptr/main/man/figures/logo.png" align="right" width="120" height="139" alt="gptr logo"/></picture>

gptr runs language model agents in your current R session. Agents can analyze objects
already in memory and create R objects that you can inspect, reuse or modify.

- **Work with live R objects.** Continue an analysis across prompts using the same data and
  intermediate results.
- **Use agents or typed decisions.** Conversational models return an agent session; decision
  models return R vectors of logical answers, labels or scores.
- **Keep a record you can rerun.** Record agent calls and their executed R code alongside
  your analysis, then replay the code with the required inputs and packages.

## Installation

gptr requires R 4.2 or later and has no compiled code. This README describes version 1.0.0.

**Development version from GitHub:**

```{r, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Broccolito/gptr@main")
```

**Released version from CRAN:**

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("gptr")
```

Choose one route. If `packageVersion("gptr")` is below 1.0.0, install from GitHub before
following these examples. After installation, load the package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(gptr)
```

## Connect a model

Choose one of the following routes before running the analysis examples.

**API key.** Put your provider's key in a private `.env` file. For example, the Anthropic
route needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gptr_env("~/keys/.env")
gptr_config(model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5", .scope = "user")
```

This saves the default model for future R sessions. Use `.scope = "session"` to limit a
setting to the current R process. `gptr_providers()` lists configured routes.

**Existing CLI login.** Install and sign in to Claude Code or Codex outside R, then open
the chat:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
peter()
```

With no default model set, the console offers the available CLI routes and saves your
choice. Enter `/exit` to return to R. CLI sign-in is separate from API credentials.

**Local Ollama model.** Start Ollama separately and install a chat model that supports tool
calls. Select an installed model, for example:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gptr_config(model = "ollama/qwen3:1.7b", .scope = "session")
```

gptr does not install Ollama or download models. Local-only inference is on by default;
a workflow remains local only when every model and tool it uses is local.

The first interactive use of a remote provider asks you to acknowledge the data it receives.
See [Language models](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/language-models.html) for
provider setup and supported routes.

## Run an analysis

With a model configured, ask for a task and continue the same agent session:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
session = peter("Fit mpg on wt in mtcars and store the model as fit.", mtcars)
session |> peter("Which cars have the largest residuals in fit?")
session$text
coef(fit)
```

The pipe adds a turn to the same conversation and reuses `fit`. The returned objects have
different roles:

| Object | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `session` | The agent conversation, status and usage, as a `gptr_session` |
| `session$text` | The latest text answer |
| `fit` | The fitted R model, available in your workspace |

`session$value` holds the most recent R result selected with `gptr_return()`; a turn that
selects no result leaves that value unchanged.

At the console, agent code runs in your R workspace. R computes on the full objects, while
the model receives size-limited descriptions, previews and tool output that may include
data values. R's usual memory allocation and copy-on-modify rules apply. See
[Execution model](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/execution-model.html) and
[Data sent to providers](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/reference/gptr_egress.html).

In the default `manual` mode, actions classified as read-only run directly; actions classified
as changes ask for approval unless an existing rule allows them. The check is advisory and
provides no sandbox; see
[Security considerations](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/reference/gptr_security.html)
or `?gptr_security` in R.

## Record and replay an analysis

Choose a recording file before starting the calls you want to keep. This example records a
new analysis using R's built-in `mtcars` data:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gptr_doc("analysis.R")
session = peter("Fit mpg on wt in mtcars and store the model as fit.")
session |> peter("Summarize the residuals in fit.")
gptr_doc(FALSE)
```

gptr writes eligible top-level calls and their executed R code into `analysis.R`, with
model and execution metadata. These are local files you can review and version with your
analysis. In a new R session, replay the recorded code:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(gptr)
gptr_source("analysis.R", replay = "replay")
```

Replay makes no model calls. It executes the recorded R code, including its side effects,
and requires that code's input data, files and packages.

To ask the model again, use `gptr_source("analysis.R", replay = "live")`. The new run can
produce different code or results. `gptr_export()` can turn an eligible recorded `.R` file
into an ordinary R script.

Recording also supports R Markdown, Quarto and Jupyter. See
[Record, replay and export](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/script-as-history.html)
for document setup, recording limits and export requirements.

## Return typed decisions

A decision model returns one answer per input: a logical value, a label selected with
`choices`, or a numeric score defined by `levels`. The selected model type determines
whether `peter()` returns a decision vector or an agent session.

This example uses hosted Jev and requires `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, which `gptr_env()` can load
from your key file:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
abstracts = c("We randomized 200 adults to drug or placebo.",
              "We followed 5000 nurses for 20 years.")
is_rct = peter("Is this a randomized trial?", abstracts, model = "jev")
is_rct
gptr_prob(is_rct)
```

`is_rct` is a logical vector. Here, `gptr_prob()` returns the model's probability of `TRUE`
for each abstract. It does not establish the probability that a classification is correct.

Local Clef and Clef Flash provide typed decisions through Ollama 0.35.1 or later.
gptr calls typed decision models **System 1** and conversational agents **System 2**.
See [Typed decisions](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/system-one.html) for
scores, uncertainty, calibration and a complete offline example.

## Learn more

Start with [Getting started](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/getting-started.html);
its examples run offline with a scripted `gptr_fake_provider()`.
In R, open it with `vignette("getting-started", package = "gptr")`.

- [Interactive console](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/interactive-console.html):
  chat, commands and instructions sent while an agent works.
- [Configuration](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/configuration.html):
  defaults, scopes and permissions.
- [Function reference](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/reference/index.html) and
  [cheat sheet](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/cheatsheet.html).

## Why Peter?

The name honors Peter Naur's work on readable language definitions and Peter Cathcart
Wason's research with Jonathan Evans on reasoning. System 1 and System 2 name software
roles in gptr; they imply nothing about human cognition. See
[Why Peter?](https://broccolito.github.io/gptr/articles/why-peter.html) for the history and sources.

## Upgrading from gptr 0.7.0

gptr 1.0.0 is a rewrite. `get_response()` and `dataframe_to_text()` were removed: use
`peter("your prompt")$text` and pass a data frame to `peter()` as context.
See [NEWS.md](https://github.com/Broccolito/gptr/blob/main/NEWS.md).

## Installation troubleshooting

If pak reports `Subprocess is busy or cannot start`, or loading gptr reports a missing or
corrupt `gptr.rdb`, restart R and reinstall before loading the package. You can also install
from GitHub with `remotes::install_github("Broccolito/gptr")` if remotes is installed.

## License and acknowledgments

gptr is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. Third-party notices are in
[inst/COPYRIGHTS](https://github.com/Broccolito/gptr/blob/main/inst/COPYRIGHTS).

gptr was inspired by Mario Zechner's 'pi' coding agent. The tool descriptions, edit guidelines
and prompt-template grammar are derived from 'pi', the model catalog from models.dev and the
secret patterns from gitleaks, and the System 1 emulation prompt follows TypeSafe AI's
system-one-adapter-python. All four are MIT-licensed. Ideas came from 'ellmer', 'tidyllm',
'btw' and 'mcptools', none of which gptr depends on. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, TypeSafe AI,
Ollama and the vendors of the command-line tools are third-party services; gptr is not
affiliated with or endorsed by them.
